# Welcome to our community stories.

## We love sharing the stories of our community members. Do you have a story you would like to contribute to our blog?

Pitch your story to [communications@cwb.org](mailto:acoumou@cwb.org).

## Building a Chesapeake Light Craft: We survived "boat camp"!

### By Shelley Sabin

![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/9cad6e8b-46f6-458b-9d30-62f940105f21/Pasted+Graphic+4.jpg)

Shelley and her friend Bryan spent 5½ days at one of CWB's [Chesapeake Light Craft workshops](https://www.cwb.org/chesapeake-light-craft-boatbuilding-classes) at [CWB's boathouse at the historic Cama Beach](https://www.cwb.org/cama-todo) on Camano Island, building a Jimmy Skiff II. The week covered sanding, epoxy work, fiberglassing, flotation foam and seat installation — plus one mishap where a stir stick got epoxied to the hull. She plans to finish the boat before crabbing season and recommends the workshop, especially to beginners.

## You Can't Go Sailing Without Sails

### By marty johnson

![A volunteer demonstrates how to backsplice the end of a line](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1624052486927-LCS15X8L37YLQGFN07HL/Marty.png)

The volunteer sail team inspects, repairs, and makes sails for CWB's livery fleet — more than 200 sails. The team moved from cold, uninsulated warehouse space to the cork-floored sail loft in the Wagner Education Center. Marty walks through the sailmaking process and upcoming projects, including sails for a Hvalsoe 16 and replacement mainsails for the Blanchard Junior Knockabouts.

![Volunteer lays out a sail in the CWB sail loft](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1624052830597-GCBC5XAHSXRP0QLBCTL2/Marty8-edited.png)
![Volunteers test out the sail for the Kitten](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1624052888644-S2JRART70YPZBDG25UAD/Marty9.JPG)

## If I'm Going to Build a Boat, I Might As Well Learn How to Sail One

### By Brian stack

![Brian Stack and friend prepare a sailboat to depart the dock](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1619809217317-0V1ZLN2S9FYTKCEZ5GOT/8C607C70-FC61-4962-B906-41FBF1DE8584.jpeg)

Inspired by *The Woodwright's Shop* and Leo Goolden's restoration of the yacht *Tally Ho* (watch [here](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCg-_lYeV8hBnDSay7nmphUA)), Brian took up woodworking and found CWB. He completed SailNOW!, now volunteers at the livery helping with peapod rentals, and plans to build a stitch-and-glue pram.

![Roy Underhill at the Woodwright's Shop on PBS.](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1619809646581-RZV6IX75K7KTO8AHCHEV/mezzanine_352.jpeg)
![Leo Goolden works on English sailing yacht TALLY HO](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1619809797703-YXPSYB2490RUJ6M2QXVU/image.jpeg)

## The Journey to Hand-building My Chesapeake Light Craft

### By Mary Sue Galvin

![Closeup of a freshly varnished bow of a boat](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1614371764234-7XWLC8TEWOS4RULKELTK/IMG_8058+%281%29.jpg)

A retired nurse practitioner who has lived on a Lake Union houseboat since 1986, Mary Sue was inspired by her grandfather's handmade tools to learn woodworking. After sailing lessons at CWB she took a Chesapeake Light Craft class taught by Casey Wilkinson — one of the classes CWB [regularly hosts in the Wagner Education Center on the South Lake Union campus in Seattle.](https://www.cwb.org/woodworking) — built her own boat, and plans to volunteer at CWB this summer.

![IMG_3341.jpg](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1614371664282-19IS75YFTEKHAD2TL8PK/IMG_3341.jpg)
